# Experiment 0025 — Real teams change everything except the answer

**Date:** 2026-08-31
**Result: the pool was replaced, the agent's behaviour changed completely, and the conclusion it was supposed to overturn survived intact.** Teams are now harvested from the replay corpus instead of generated by a singles format. The agent's status-move rate went from 2.2% of its choices to 30.3% against a human 34.0% — **with no agent code changed at all**. Then 0023's tenure A/B, re-run on the new pool under two calibrations, came back **+0.8 and +0.2 points**, against +0.9 on the old pool. Three independent nulls across two distributions.

## The pool

0024 established the problem: `gen9championsrandombattle` carries no `gameType` and is therefore a singles generator, and Champions ships no random doubles generator. `champions_ai.data.harvest` replaces it with real teams — the six Pokemon each replay names, with sets pooled across the corpus, built from the **train split only** because the corpus also supplies the agreement benchmarks.

Three things the engine rejected on the way, each a real fact about replay data:

- **Item Clause.** Sitrus Berry and Focus Sash announce themselves *when consumed*, so they dominate the observed evidence and every species independently answered "Sitrus Berry". Items are now chosen against what the rest of the team holds.
- **`|-ability|` reports the ability that is active**, which after Trace, Skill Swap or Mummy belongs to somebody else. Believing it put Pixilate and Fairy Aura on Pokemon that cannot have them. Only abilities the species owns are believed; Showdown's curated sets fill the gap, since most abilities never announce.
- **A fourth of teams could not be completed** and are dropped rather than shipped with a Pokemon that can only Struggle.

752 of 783 pass `validate_team`. 295 distinct rosters across 752 teams, which is repetition that belongs there — the real meta repeats archetypes, and Kingambit lands on 41.8% of them because it lands on 41.8% of real teams.

## What it did to the agent, with nothing changed in the agent

```
                                  old pool   harvested   humans
  status share of move choices        2.2%       30.3%    34.0%
  status picked when available        2.5%       24.7%        -
  Protect chances per battle          0.40       17.22        -
  Protect taken when available       10.0%       24.1%        -
  battle length, median turns          8.5        12.0        -
  mean tenure                         2.94        4.77        -
  T > 2 (where setup pays off)       44.6%       65.5%        -
  agent errors                           -           0        -
```

**0023's headline was the pool, not the agent.** "The agent almost never picks status moves" was true and the explanation was wrong: it had almost no status moves. Given real ones it picks them at close to the human rate without a line changing. It also uses Trick Room and Rage Powder without error, which is worth noting precisely because **redirection is not modelled at all** — those are falling through to the generic support value.

## The calibration is not a constant

0023 fitted tenure as `T = 1 + raw/0.5`, pinned at the bottom for safety. Refitted on harvested teams:

```
fitted on harvested teams:  T = 3.66 + 1.24 * raw   (residual sd 4.12)
fitted on the old pool:     T = 1.96 + 1.05 * raw
shipped (0023)              T = 1.00 + 2.00 * raw
```

The intercept nearly quadrupled. A "constant" that moves that far between team distributions is not a constant — it says `_incoming_threat`, a worst-case max over both opponents' moves, is a poor tenure proxy exactly where Protect and redirection stop the worst case from landing. The residual of 4.12 against a mean of 4.72 says the same thing: it ranks, it does not measure.

That is why both calibrations were run. Testing only the shipped one would test a model known to be wrong here; testing only the refitted one would leave it unclear whether any gain came from the idea or from the constants.

## The A/B

```
as shipped  (T = 1.00 + 2.00*raw)
    seed 1    389/800  = 48.6%
    seed 7    424/800  = 53.0%
    pooled    813/1600 = 50.8%   95% CI 48.4%-53.3%   z = +0.65, p = 0.52

refitted    (T = 3.66 + 1.24*raw)
    seed 1    388/800  = 48.5%
    seed 7    415/800  = 51.9%
    pooled    803/1600 = 50.2%   95% CI 47.7%-52.6%   z = +0.15, p = 0.88

0023, old pool                     = 50.9%   95% CI 48.4%-53.3%   p = 0.48
```

Three measurements, two team distributions, two calibrations, 4,800 battles. All null. The correctly-calibrated arm is if anything the flattest of the three.

**`tenure_boosts` stays off.** This is now a well-supported negative rather than an underpowered one: a null that survives a distribution shift this large — battles 40% longer, tenure 62% higher, status moves 14 times more available — is much stronger evidence than the original.

## What this settles

- **Pricing offensive setup by tenure is not worth points.** Asked three ways, answered the same way each time. The idea was sound arithmetic and the game does not reward it.
- **The pool was hiding a large behavioural difference and not hiding this one.** Worth holding both facts at once: 0024 was a real and serious measurement error, *and* correcting it did not overturn the conclusion drawn under it. Finding a flaw in an instrument is not the same as finding the previous answer wrong.
- **Every self-play number before 0024 still needs re-checking on its own.** This one survived; 0020's exchange rate, 0021's evaluator grading and 0022's search result have not been re-run.

## Not established

- Whether redirection matters. Rage Powder is on 36% of harvested teams, Follow Me on 9%, and neither is modelled. The agent has never been measured against an opponent using them.
- Whether the harvested sets are good enough for finer questions. Stat spreads and natures are invented (11 uniform, neutral), Protect lands on 100% of teams which is likely over-assigned per-Pokemon, and species the corpus barely saw are dropped.
- Whether more replays change anything. Collection toward 2,000 is running; species coverage saturated at 148 by 500, so it buys set variety rather than breadth.
